title: ANDS Studio — Dossier manager (all products in submission)
walkthrough:
The dossier catalog page opens with a top bar. On the left is a brand mark — a small dot followed by "ANDS Studio" with the smaller suffix "· dossier manager". On the right sit a user chip and several link chips (Help, Portfolio, Registry, Correspondence, and a guided-journey link).

Below the bar, the page heading reads "Your product dossiers". On the same line, to the right, are: a two-button view toggle with "Grid" and "List" (Grid selected by default); a "View archived (trash)" button (which becomes "Hide archived" once expanded); and a "New dossier +" button. An explanatory paragraph follows: "A Dossier ID is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada. Open a dossier to build its eCTD Module 1–5 — upload or author every document with full guidance on each section. Everything on this page belongs to your workspace alone: client workspaces are isolated end-to-end (per-workspace data partitions, tenant-checked on every request, cross-client access is structurally impossible)." Several phrases in that sentence — "Dossier ID", "eCTD", and "Module 1–5" — are rendered as glossary term components.

Clicking "New dossier +" changes that button's label to "Cancel" and reveals a card headed "New dossier". The first row has two input fields side by side: "Dossier ID" with placeholder text "e123456", and "Product name" with placeholder text "Drugazole 10 mg tablet". Directly under the Dossier ID field is a small note: "Format: one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456). A d… placeholder marks a draft ID until Health Canada issues the real one." A second row of fields follows: a "Submission type" dropdown whose options are "ANDS — Abbreviated New Drug Submission (generic)", "SANDS — Supplement to an ANDS (post-NOC change)", and "SNDS — Supplement to a New Drug Submission" (ANDS selected by default); when ANDS is selected, a checkbox appears beneath it, labeled "Comparative-BE only (CS-BE path — suppresses the nonclinical/clinical summaries)", checked by default. Alongside are two optional fields: "Client / sponsor (optional)" with placeholder "Acme Pharma Inc.", and "Owner (PM) (optional)" with placeholder "j.smith@cro.example".

Below the fields is a note: "Health Canada issues your Dossier ID when you file a Dossier ID Request through REP (via your CESG account)." followed by an inline button, "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →", and the sentence "You can set the real ID any time; validation reminds you before filing." Clicking the placeholder button fills the Dossier ID field with a generated ID: the letter "d" followed by six random digits. A code comment states the convention: the 'd' prefix means draft — work starts now, and the real Health Canada ID replaces it later.

The card's action button reads "Create & open →". If the entered ID does not match the required pattern (one lowercase letter followed by 6–7 digits), an error notice appears: "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". While creation is in progress the button is disabled and its label changes to "Creating…". On success a toast confirms "Dossier {id} created" and the browser navigates straight into the new dossier's Module 1 workspace. Any API error is shown in a red-styled notice containing the raw error text.

Below the create area, the list itself has states. While fetching, the page shows the muted text "Loading dossiers…". If the workspace has no dossiers, a notice reads "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." Otherwise, a triage bar appears first: a filter input with placeholder "Filter by product, ID, type, client or owner…", a "Just my dossiers" checkbox (shown when the current user's email is known), and a muted "N of M" count of how many dossiers match. If a filter excludes everything, a notice reads "No dossiers match your filter."

In the default Grid view, a grid of tiles appears, one per dossier. Each tile is itself a link that opens that dossier's Module 1 page. A tile shows: the dossier ID; the product title; a meta line showing the submission type (for a comparative-BE ANDS the type is shown as "ANDS · CS-BE", otherwise just the plain type such as "ANDS", "SANDS", or "SNDS"), with the client/sponsor appended after " · " when one is set; a horizontal progress bar whose fill width is the fraction of applicable modules that have passed; and a status chip. The status chip never says "Ready to file" — deliberately, per an in-code comment, because module completeness is not a filing verdict. When the dossier's gate is complete the chip reads a count like "3/9 modules built — validate to file" (passed over applicable), with a tooltip explaining this is structural completeness only, not a validation pass; otherwise it reads just "3/9 modules built" with a tooltip "Some required modules are not yet built". Each tile also has an "✕" delete button in the corner, with tooltip "Delete" plus the dossier ID and an accessible label of the form "Delete dossier" plus the ID.

If a dossier's ID starts with "d" — the placeholder convention — an extra chip-style button appears next to the ID on its tile, labeled "⚠ placeholder — set real ID ✎", with the tooltip "Placeholder ID — NOT a Health Canada Dossier ID. Export and transmission are blocked until you set the real ID (issued via REP)." Clicking it opens an in-app modal (the shared "set real Dossier ID" dialog) for entering the real Health Canada Dossier ID; on success the list reloads. Both the placeholder button and the delete button intercept the click so the tile link does not navigate.

Clicking a tile's "✕" opens an in-app modal titled "Delete this dossier?" — not a native browser confirm, and not a permanent deletion. Its body explains this does NOT permanently destroy the dossier: it moves the dossier and all of its documents to the archive (trash), where it can be restored with undo, and the action is recorded on the append-only audit trail. To proceed the user must type the exact Dossier ID to confirm and enter a required "Reason for change" (placeholder "e.g. duplicate created in error"); the action button reads "Archive dossier" (and "Archiving…" while in progress) and stays disabled until both are provided. On success a toast confirms the dossier was archived and recoverable from Trash, and the list reloads.

There is also a "List" view (via the Grid/List toggle) that renders the same dossiers as a sortable table with columns Dossier ID, Product, Status, Type, Client / sponsor, Owner, and Soonest due (each header is a sort button), plus a per-row delete "✕"; placeholder-ID rows show a "⚠ placeholder" chip. Expanding "View archived (trash)" reveals an "Archived (recoverable)" section explaining that deleting archives rather than destroys, listing each archived dossier with its archive time / who / reason and a "Restore ↩" button.

Opening a tile (or visiting a bare dossier URL, which redirects to Module 1) lands in the dossier workspace. Its own top bar replaces the catalog bar. On the left, "ANDS Studio" is now a link back to the catalog, followed by a small suffix showing the dossier's title, or its ID if no title is loaded. Next to that is a tab strip (accessible label "eCTD modules") with five tabs: "M1" through "M5". Each tab carries a small state marker: a check icon if that module's checks pass (complete), a warning-triangle icon if the module holds an unconfirmed sample/AI draft that needs review, "—" if the module is not applicable, and a dot otherwise (in progress or not started); tabs also show a "filled/total" required-section fraction and a small completeness underline bar, and the tab for the module currently open is marked active. To the right of the tabs are the user chip and four link chips: "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio", and "Journey" — the first two link within the current dossier (its viewer and audit pages), the last two lead back out to the portfolio and the guided journey home page.

Immediately under this workspace top bar, if the dossier's ID is a placeholder (starts with "d"), a persistent warning strip appears: "This dossier uses a placeholder ID ({id}). Set the real Health Canada Dossier ID (issued via REP) before validation / export — export stays blocked until you do.", with a "Set real Dossier ID" button that opens the same set-real-ID modal. (A second persistent strip warns, in red, when a signed package is no longer cleanly signed and must be re-signed, but that only appears once a signature has gone stale or conflicted.)
